question.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\frac{2}{{x}^{2}},\,1\le x\le 2.
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{5}].$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the fifth raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{5}] & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{5}\cdot \frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{4}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(16-1) \\  & =\frac{15}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
